A desktop PC is left out on purpose. It is mostly built from parts, so it has no model name of its own to write.

```javascript
import { randDevice } from 'randino';

randDevice();
// ['Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra']
```

## Options

Every option is optional, and the defaults are what the empty call above uses.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `DeviceTypeOption` | `'all'` | `phone`, `tablet` or `laptop`, or several of them. See [what it draws from](https://randino.cdget.com/device/rand-device#catalog). |
| `minYear` | `number` | `—` | The earliest year a device may have been released in. See [years](https://randino.cdget.com/device/rand-device#years). |
| `maxYear` | `number` | `—` | The latest year a device may have been released in. See [years](https://randino.cdget.com/device/rand-device#years). |
| `includeVendor` | `boolean` | `true` | Write the maker in front of the model. See [makers and models](https://randino.cdget.com/device/rand-device#vendor). |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many devices to return. Clamped to `0` … `10000`. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same device twice. Returns fewer than `count` once the catalog runs out. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or a `DeviceDetail` per device. Dart has no such parameter — see [the detail output](https://randino.cdget.com/device/rand-device#the-detail-output). |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from — see [Choosing the source](https://randino.cdget.com/guide/getting-started#choosing-the-source). Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |

```javascript
randDevice({ type: 'laptop', count: 2 });
// ['Lenovo ThinkPad T14 Gen 3', 'Apple MacBook Air (M2, 2022)']

randDevice({ type: ['phone', 'tablet'], count: 3 });
// ['Google Pixel 8', 'Apple iPad (10th generation)', 'Sony Xperia 1 V']
```

## What it draws from {#catalog}

459 models from the first iPhone in 2007 to the devices released by the end of 2025, every one of them as likely as the next once `type` and the years have narrowed them:

| Type | Models | Years | Makers |
| --- | --: | --- | --- |
| `phone` | 260 | 2007 – 2025 | Apple, Samsung, Google, Xiaomi, OnePlus, Sony, LG, Huawei, Motorola, Nothing, Nokia, HTC, BlackBerry |
| `tablet` | 99 | 2010 – 2025 | Apple, Samsung, Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Lenovo, Xiaomi, Huawei |
| `laptop` | 100 | 2008 – 2025 | Apple, Microsoft, Dell, Lenovo, HP, ASUS, Samsung, Razer, Google, LG |

A model is written the way its maker writes it. Apple's iPads and Macs carry the identifier Apple gives them, generation and all — `iPad (10th generation)`, `iPad Pro 13-inch (M4)`, `MacBook Air (M2, 2022)` — a ThinkPad its `Gen`, an EliteBook its `G`, and a laptop line that keeps one name across years the year it is told apart by: `ROG Zephyrus G14 (2023)`, `Blade 15 (2020)`. A detachable two-in-one such as the Surface Pro is a tablet, and the Surface Laptop a laptop.

The year is the year the device was first released. A phone launched in one market a few weeks before the rest is dated by that first market, so a Xiaomi or OnePlus flagship launched in China in December is that December's year.

The names are the products' own, and they belong to their owners. randino is not affiliated with any of them.

## Makers and models {#vendor}

The maker goes in front of the model by default, so a result reads the way a spec sheet or an inventory writes it. A model whose name already opens on its maker's — `Xiaomi 14`, `OnePlus 12`, `Nothing Phone (2)` — is never written with the maker twice. `includeVendor: false` writes the model alone.

```javascript
randDevice({ type: 'phone', count: 3 }); // ['Apple iPhone 13', 'Xiaomi 14', 'Google Pixel 7a']
randDevice({ type: 'phone', includeVendor: false, count: 3 }); // ['iPhone 13', 'Xiaomi 14', 'Pixel 7a']
```

## Years {#years}

`minYear` and `maxYear` keep to the devices released in that range, both years included, so `maxYear: 2012` is what was on sale by the end of 2012. A range nothing was released in is answered with nothing rather than with a device from outside it, and a range the wrong way round keeps `maxYear`.

```javascript
randDevice({ type: 'phone', maxYear: 2012, count: 3 });
// ['Apple iPhone 4', 'Samsung Galaxy S III', 'HTC Dream']

randDevice({ type: 'laptop', minYear: 2024, count: 2 });
// ['Apple MacBook Air (13-inch, M4, 2025)', 'Lenovo ThinkPad T14 Gen 5']
```

The same years on [`randOs`](https://randino.cdget.com/os/rand-os#years) draw the systems that were out alongside them, so a sample machine can be put together from one year.

## The detail output {#the-detail-output}

The detail carries the maker and the model apart, so a result can be stored in two columns while the whole name is shown.

```javascript
randDevice({ output: 'detail' });
// [{ device: 'Google Pixel 8', vendor: 'Google', model: 'Pixel 8', type: 'phone', year: 2023 }]
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device` | `string` | The device, as the value form returns it. |
| `vendor` | `string` | Who makes it: `Apple`, `Samsung`, `Lenovo`. |
| `model` | `string` | The model's own name: `Galaxy S24 Ultra`. |
| `type` | `DeviceType` | `phone`, `tablet` or `laptop`. |
| `year` | `number` | The year the device was released. |

## See also

- [`randOs`](https://randino.cdget.com/os/rand-os) — an operating system to run on it, from the same years.
- [`randCpu`](https://randino.cdget.com/cpu/rand-cpu) — the processor inside it.
- [`randRam`](https://randino.cdget.com/ram/rand-ram) — the memory it comes with.
- [`randResolution`](https://randino.cdget.com/resolution/rand-resolution) — the size of its screen.

---

# randRam

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/ram/rand-ram

Generates amounts of memory and returns `count` of them, written the way a spec sheet writes them: `16 GB`, `8 GB`, `512 MB`. Every size is one a phone, a laptop, a desktop or a workstation is really sold with, drawn by [how common it is](https://randino.cdget.com/ram/rand-ram#sizes), so a sample is mostly 8 and 16 GB. A size is only ever written in a [unit](https://randino.cdget.com/ram/rand-ram#units) it is a whole number of, so no result carries a decimal point.

A size has no language, so `randRam` takes none.

```javascript
import { randRam } from 'randino';

randRam();
// ['16 GB']
```

## Options

Every option is optional, and the defaults are what the empty call above uses.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unit` | `RamUnitOption` | `'auto'` | `MB` or `GB`, or `'auto'` for the largest unit each size is a whole number of. See [units](https://randino.cdget.com/ram/rand-ram#units). |
| `includeUnit` | `boolean` | `true` | Write the unit after the number. |
| `minSize` | `number` | `—` | The smallest size to return. See [bounds](https://randino.cdget.com/ram/rand-ram#bounds). |
| `maxSize` | `number` | `—` | The largest size to return. See [bounds](https://randino.cdget.com/ram/rand-ram#bounds). |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many sizes to return. Clamped to `0` … `10000`. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same size twice. Returns fewer than `count` once the sizes run out. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or a `RamDetail` per size. Dart has no such parameter — see [the detail output](https://randino.cdget.com/ram/rand-ram#the-detail-output). |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from — see [Choosing the source](https://randino.cdget.com/guide/getting-started#choosing-the-source). Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |

## How often each size comes up {#sizes}

The pool holds every amount of memory a machine is commonly sold with, from the 512 MB of an early smartphone to the terabyte of a workstation, and each one comes up in proportion to how common it is. The shares are written by hand in the order the sizes are common in, not measured from any one survey:

| Size                            |         Share |
| ------------------------------- | ------------: |
| 8 GB                            |         20.2% |
| 16 GB                           |         18.5% |
| 4 GB, 32 GB                     |    10.1% each |
| 12 GB                           |          8.4% |
| 6 GB                            |          6.7% |
| 2 GB, 64 GB                     |     4.2% each |
| 3 GB, 24 GB                     |     3.4% each |
| 1 GB                            |          2.5% |
| 512 MB, 48 GB, 128 GB           |     1.7% each |
| 18 GB, 36 GB, 96 GB             |     0.8% each |
| 192 GB, 256 GB, 512 GB, 1024 GB | 0.8% together |

The odd sizes are real too: 3 and 6 GB phones, the 18 and 36 GB of a Mac with an M3 Pro or M3 Max, and the 24 and 48 GB of a laptop with two modules of different sizes.

## Units {#units}

Memory counts in powers of two, so a gigabyte here is 1024 megabytes, the way an operating system reports it. Left to `'auto'`, each size is written in the largest unit it is a whole number of: `16 GB`, but `512 MB`. A unit you name keeps to the sizes that are a whole number of it, so `GB` leaves 512 MB out rather than writing `0.5 GB`, and `MB` writes every size, 16 GB as `16384 MB`.

`includeUnit: false` writes the number alone. Without a unit beside it a bare `512` and a bare `16` could not be told apart, so a size written bare is in gigabytes unless you name `MB`.

```javascript
randRam({ count: 3 }); // ['8 GB', '16 GB', '4 GB']
randRam({ unit: 'MB', count: 2 }); // ['8192 MB', '16384 MB']
randRam({ includeUnit: false, count: 3 }); // ['16', '8', '32']
```

## Bounds {#bounds}

`minSize` and `maxSize` keep to the sizes between them, both ends included. They are read in the unit you name, and in gigabytes when the unit is left to fit, so `minSize: 16` is 16 GB and up while `unit: 'MB', maxSize: 4096` is 4096 MB and down. A bound need not be whole: `maxSize: 0.5` is 512 MB and down.

A range no real size is inside is answered with nothing rather than with a size nobody sells, and a range the wrong way round keeps `maxSize`, the bound a caller is usually holding to.

```javascript
randRam({ minSize: 16, maxSize: 64, count: 3 }); // ['32 GB', '16 GB', '64 GB']
randRam({ unit: 'MB', maxSize: 4096, count: 2 }); // ['2048 MB', '4096 MB']
randRam({ minSize: 5, maxSize: 5 }); // []
```

## The detail output {#the-detail-output}

The detail carries the number and the unit apart, and the same size in bytes, so a result can be compared and sorted whatever unit it was written in.

```javascript
randRam({ output: 'detail' });
// [{ ram: '16 GB', value: 16, unit: 'GB', bytes: 17179869184 }]
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ram` | `string` | The size, as the value form returns it. |
| `value` | `number` | The number written: `16`. |
| `unit` | `RamUnit` | `MB` or `GB`. |
| `bytes` | `number` | The same size in bytes, counted in powers of two: 16 GB is `17179869184`. |

## See also

- [`randDevice`](https://randino.cdget.com/device/rand-device) — a phone, a tablet or a laptop to put the memory in.
- [`randDiskType`](https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-type) and [`randDiskSize`](https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-size) — the storage beside it.
- [`randOs`](https://randino.cdget.com/os/rand-os) — the operating system it runs.

---

# randDiskType

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-type

Generates the kind of storage a machine has and returns `count` of them, written the way a spec sheet labels it: `SSD`, `HDD`, `UFS`. Each kind comes up by [how common it is](https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-type#kinds) on the platform it is drawn for, so a desktop is mostly an SSD and a phone mostly UFS. With [`output: 'detail'`](https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-type#the-detail-output) it reports the code and the name behind each label.

A label is the same in every language, so `randDiskType` takes none.

```javascript
import { randDiskType } from 'randino';

randDiskType();
// ['SSD']
```

## Options

Every option is optional, and the defaults are what the empty call above uses.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `platform` | `SystemPlatformOption` | `'all'` | `desktop` for a PC, a laptop included, `mobile` for a phone or a tablet. `'all'` draws from both. |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many labels to return. Clamped to `0` … `10000`. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same label twice. Returns fewer than `count` once the labels run out. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or a `DiskTypeDetail` per result. Dart has no such parameter — see [the detail output](https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-type#the-detail-output). |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from — see [Choosing the source](https://randino.cdget.com/guide/getting-started#choosing-the-source). Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |

## The kinds {#kinds}

Five kinds of storage, each with the share it comes up at on the platform that uses it. The shares are written by hand in the order the kinds are common in, not measured from any one survey:

| Code   | Label | Name                     | `desktop` | `mobile` |
| ------ | ----- | ------------------------ | --------: | -------: |
| `ssd`  | SSD   | Solid State Drive        |       62% |        — |
| `hdd`  | HDD   | Hard Disk Drive          |       33% |        — |
| `sshd` | SSHD  | Solid State Hybrid Drive |        3% |        — |
| `emmc` | eMMC  | Embedded MultiMediaCard  |        2% |      30% |
| `ufs`  | UFS   | Universal Flash Storage  |         — |      70% |

An SSD covers flash behind SATA and behind NVMe alike, the way a spec sheet's storage line does. eMMC is soldered flash: it is what older phones and cheap tablets store to, and what a low-cost laptop is built with, so both platforms draw it. With `platform: 'all'` the platform is picked first, so desktop and mobile storage come up about evenly.

```javascript
randDiskType({ platform: 'desktop', count: 3 }); // ['SSD', 'HDD', 'SSD']
randDiskType({ platform: 'mobile', count: 3 }); // ['UFS', 'eMMC', 'UFS']
randDiskType({ unique: true, count: 10 }); // ['SSD', 'UFS', 'HDD', 'eMMC', 'SSHD']
```

## The detail output {#the-detail-output}

The detail carries the code beside the label, so you can store `ssd` and show `SSD`, and the name the label stands for.

```javascript
randDiskType({ output: 'detail' });
// [{ diskType: 'SSD', code: 'ssd', name: 'Solid State Drive', platform: 'desktop' }]
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `diskType` | `string` | The label, as the value form returns it. |
| `code` | `DiskType` | `hdd`, `ssd`, `sshd`, `emmc` or `ufs`. |
| `name` | `string` | The label written out: `Solid State Drive`. |
| `platform` | `SystemPlatform` | The kind of machine it was drawn for. |

## See also

- [`randDevice`](https://randino.cdget.com/device/rand-device) — a phone, a tablet or a laptop to put the storage in.
- [`randDiskSize`](https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-size) — how much the drive holds.
- [`randRam`](https://randino.cdget.com/ram/rand-ram) — the memory beside it.

---

# randDiskSize

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-size

Generates drive capacities and returns `count` of them, written the way a box or a spec sheet writes them: `512 GB`, `1 TB`, `4 TB`. Every size is one a drive or a phone's storage is really sold with, drawn by [how common it is](https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-size#sizes), so a sample is mostly 256 GB, 512 GB and 1 TB. A size is only ever written in a [unit](https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-size#units) it is a whole number of, so no result carries a decimal point.

A size has no language, so `randDiskSize` takes none.

```javascript
import { randDiskSize } from 'randino';

randDiskSize();
// ['512 GB']
```

## Options

Every option is optional, and the defaults are what the empty call above uses.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unit` | `DiskUnitOption` | `'auto'` | `MB`, `GB` or `TB`, or `'auto'` for the largest unit each size is a whole number of. See [units](https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-size#units). |
| `includeUnit` | `boolean` | `true` | Write the unit after the number. |
| `minSize` | `number` | `—` | The smallest size to return. See [bounds](https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-size#bounds). |
| `maxSize` | `number` | `—` | The largest size to return. See [bounds](https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-size#bounds). |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many sizes to return. Clamped to `0` … `10000`. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same size twice. Returns fewer than `count` once the sizes run out. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or a `DiskSizeDetail` per size. Dart has no such parameter — see [the detail output](https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-size#the-detail-output). |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from — see [Choosing the source](https://randino.cdget.com/guide/getting-started#choosing-the-source). Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |

## How often each size comes up {#sizes}

The pool holds every capacity a drive or a phone's storage is commonly sold with, from the 16 GB of an early phone to a 24 TB hard disk, and each one comes up in proportion to how common it is. The shares are written by hand in the order the sizes are common in, not measured from any one survey:

| Size                                     |         Share |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------: |
| 512 GB, 1 TB                             |    15.8% each |
| 256 GB                                   |         14.1% |
| 2 TB                                     |          8.8% |
| 128 GB, 500 GB                           |     7.0% each |
| 4 TB                                     |          5.3% |
| 64 GB                                    |          3.5% |
| 240 GB, 250 GB, 480 GB, 8 TB             |     2.6% each |
| 32 GB, 120 GB, 3 TB, 6 TB                |     1.8% each |
| 16 GB, 10 TB, 12 TB                      |     0.9% each |
| 14 TB, 16 TB, 18 TB, 20 TB, 22 TB, 24 TB | 2.3% together |

The sizes a flash drive and a hard disk are each sold in are both there: 128, 256 and 512 GB for flash, 250 and 500 GB for the hard disks beside it, and the 120, 240 and 480 GB of the first SATA SSDs. Which kind of drive a machine has is [`randDiskType`](https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-type)'s to say.

## Units {#units}

A drive is sold in powers of ten, so a terabyte here is 1000 gigabytes, the way the box and the spec sheet count it — an operating system reports the same drive as a little less. Left to `'auto'`, each size is written in the largest unit it is a whole number of: `2 TB`, but `512 GB`. A unit you name keeps to the sizes that are a whole number of it, so `TB` leaves a 500 GB drive out rather than writing `0.5 TB`, and `GB` writes every size, 2 TB as `2000 GB`.

`includeUnit: false` writes the number alone. Without a unit beside it a bare `2` and a bare `512` could not be told apart, so a size written bare is in gigabytes unless you name another unit.

```javascript
randDiskSize({ count: 3 }); // ['1 TB', '256 GB', '2 TB']
randDiskSize({ unit: 'GB', count: 2 }); // ['1000 GB', '512 GB']
randDiskSize({ unit: 'TB', count: 2 }); // ['4 TB', '1 TB']
randDiskSize({ includeUnit: false, count: 3 }); // ['512', '2000', '256']
```

## Bounds {#bounds}

`minSize` and `maxSize` keep to the sizes between them, both ends included. They are read in the unit you name, and in gigabytes when the unit is left to fit, so `minSize: 1000` is 1 TB and up while `unit: 'TB', minSize: 8` is 8 TB and up. A bound need not be whole: `unit: 'TB', minSize: 1.5` is 2 TB and up.

A range no real size is inside is answered with nothing rather than with a size nobody sells, and a range the wrong way round keeps `maxSize`.

```javascript
randDiskSize({ minSize: 256, maxSize: 1000, count: 3 }); // ['512 GB', '1 TB', '256 GB']
randDiskSize({ unit: 'TB', minSize: 8, count: 2 }); // ['12 TB', '8 TB']
randDiskSize({ minSize: 600, maxSize: 900 }); // []
```

## The detail output {#the-detail-output}

The detail carries the number and the unit apart, and the same size in bytes, so a result can be compared and sorted whatever unit it was written in.

```javascript
randDiskSize({ output: 'detail' });
// [{ size: '1 TB', value: 1, unit: 'TB', bytes: 1000000000000 }]
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `string` | The size, as the value form returns it. |
| `value` | `number` | The number written: `1`. |
| `unit` | `DiskUnit` | `MB`, `GB` or `TB`. |
| `bytes` | `number` | The same size in bytes, counted in powers of ten: 1 TB is `1000000000000`. |

## See also

- [`randDiskType`](https://randino.cdget.com/disk/rand-disk-type) — the kind of drive the size belongs to.
- [`randRam`](https://randino.cdget.com/ram/rand-ram) — the memory, counted the other way, in powers of two.

---

# randCpu

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/cpu/rand-cpu

Generates real processors and returns `count` of them, each by the name its maker gave it: `Intel Core i7-13700K`, `AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D`, `Apple M3 Pro`, `Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 3`. Nothing is invented: every result is a part machines were sold with. [`platform`](https://randino.cdget.com/cpu/rand-cpu#catalog) keeps to desktop and laptop processors or to the chips of phones and tablets, and [`minYear` and `maxYear`](https://randino.cdget.com/cpu/rand-cpu#years) to the parts out in those years.

A processor is written by its own name in every language, so `randCpu` takes no `language`.

```javascript
import { randCpu } from 'randino';

randCpu();
// ['Intel Core i7-13700K']
```

## Options

Every option is optional, and the defaults are what the empty call above uses.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `platform` | `SystemPlatformOption` | `'all'` | `desktop` for desktop and laptop processors, `mobile` for the chips of phones and tablets. `'all'` draws from both. |
| `minYear` | `number` | `—` | The earliest year a processor may have come out in. See [years](https://randino.cdget.com/cpu/rand-cpu#years). |
| `maxYear` | `number` | `—` | The latest year a processor may have come out in. See [years](https://randino.cdget.com/cpu/rand-cpu#years). |
| `vendor` | `CpuVendorOption` | `'all'` | Which makers, by the name each sells under: one, several, or every one of them. See [makers](https://randino.cdget.com/cpu/rand-cpu#vendors). |
| `includeVendor` | `boolean` | `true` | Write the maker in front of the processor: `Intel Core i7-13700K` rather than `Core i7-13700K`. |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many processors to return. Clamped to `0` … `10000`. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same processor twice. Returns fewer than `count` once the catalog runs out. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or a `CpuDetail` per processor. Dart has no such parameter — see [the detail output](https://randino.cdget.com/cpu/rand-cpu#the-detail-output). |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from — see [Choosing the source](https://randino.cdget.com/guide/getting-started#choosing-the-source). Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |

```javascript
randCpu({ platform: 'desktop', count: 3 }); // ['AMD Ryzen 5 5600X', 'Intel Core i5-1135G7', 'Apple M2']
randCpu({ platform: 'mobile', count: 3 }); // ['Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 3', 'Apple A17 Pro', 'MediaTek Dimensity 9300']
randCpu({ includeVendor: false, count: 2 }); // ['Ryzen 7 7800X3D', 'Snapdragon 865']
```

## What it draws from {#catalog}

248 processors from the Pentium 4 in 2000 to the parts out by the end of 2025, every one of them as likely as the next once `platform` and the years have narrowed them:

| Platform | Maker | Parts | Years | Lines |
| --- | --- | --: | --- | --- |
| `desktop` | Intel | 82 | 2000 – 2025 | Pentium, Core 2, Core i3 to i9, Core Ultra, Celeron, Atom |
| `desktop` | AMD | 53 | 2003 – 2025 | Athlon 64, Phenom II, FX, A-Series, Ryzen, Ryzen Threadripper, Ryzen AI |
| `desktop` | Apple | 16 | 2020 – 2025 | M1 to M5, with their Pro, Max and Ultra |
| `desktop` | Qualcomm | 4 | 2022 – 2025 | Snapdragon 8cx and Snapdragon X |
| `mobile` | Apple | 25 | 2010 – 2025 | A4 to A19 Pro, the X and Z chips of the iPad included |
| `mobile` | Qualcomm | 32 | 2013 – 2025 | Snapdragon 600 to 8 Elite Gen 5 |
| `mobile` | Samsung | 12 | 2016 – 2025 | Exynos |
| `mobile` | MediaTek | 13 | 2018 – 2025 | Helio and Dimensity |
| `mobile` | Google | 5 | 2021 – 2025 | Tensor to Tensor G5 |
| `mobile` | HiSilicon | 6 | 2017 – 2024 | Kirin |

Each line is represented by the models a spec sheet most often names — the unlocked desktop part, the mainstream laptop part, the flagship and the mid-range chip of a phone line — rather than by every variant its maker sold. A laptop processor counts as `desktop`, the way a laptop runs a desktop operating system.

The names are the products' own, and they belong to their owners. randino is not affiliated with any of them.

## Makers {#vendors}

`vendor` keeps to the makers named, written as the [catalog](https://randino.cdget.com/cpu/rand-cpu#catalog) writes them: `Intel`, `AMD`, `Apple`, `Qualcomm`, `Samsung`, `MediaTek`, `Google` and `HiSilicon`, the order `CPU_VENDORS` lists them in. A name the catalog does not hold is ignored, and a list of nothing but such names draws every maker. It narrows alongside `platform` and the years, so a maker with no part there is answered with nothing: MediaTek makes no desktop processor here.

```javascript
randCpu({ vendor: 'AMD', count: 2 }); // ['AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D', 'AMD Ryzen 5 3600']
randCpu({ vendor: ['Apple', 'Qualcomm'], platform: 'desktop' }); // ['Apple M3 Pro']
randCpu({ vendor: 'MediaTek', platform: 'desktop' }); // []
```

## Years {#years}

The year of a processor is the year the first machines with it went on sale. A phone chip announced in one December and shipped in the next is the next year's, and a desktop part the year it reached the shelves. `minYear` and `maxYear` keep to the processors out in that range, both years included. A range nothing came out in is answered with nothing, and a range the wrong way round keeps `maxYear`.

```javascript
randCpu({ platform: 'desktop', maxYear: 2012, count: 3 });
// ['Intel Core i7-2600K', 'AMD Phenom II X4 940', 'Intel Core 2 Quad Q6600']

randCpu({ platform: 'mobile', minYear: 2024, count: 2 });
// ['Apple A18 Pro', 'Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite']
```

## The detail output {#the-detail-output}

The detail carries the maker and the model apart, so a result can be stored in two columns while the whole name is shown.

```javascript
randCpu({ output: 'detail' });
// [{ cpu: 'Apple M3 Pro', vendor: 'Apple', model: 'M3 Pro', platform: 'desktop', year: 2023 }]
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cpu` | `string` | The processor, as the value form returns it. |
| `vendor` | `CpuVendor` | Who makes it: `Intel`, `AMD`, `Apple`. |
| `model` | `string` | The processor's own name: `Ryzen 7 7800X3D`. |
| `platform` | `SystemPlatform` | `desktop` or `mobile`. |
| `year` | `number` | The year the first machines with it went on sale. |

## See also

- [`randDevice`](https://randino.cdget.com/device/rand-device) — a phone, a tablet or a laptop the processor could be in.
- [`randGpu`](https://randino.cdget.com/gpu/rand-gpu) — the graphics beside it.
- [`randArchitecture`](https://randino.cdget.com/architecture/rand-architecture) — the architecture it runs.
- [`randRam`](https://randino.cdget.com/ram/rand-ram) — the memory beside it.

# randGpu

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/gpu/rand-gpu

Generates real graphics processors and returns `count` of them, each by the name its maker gave it: `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090`, `AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX`, `Intel Iris Xe Graphics`, `Qualcomm Adreno 740`. Nothing is invented: every result is a part cards or machines were sold with. [`platform`](https://randino.cdget.com/gpu/rand-gpu#catalog) keeps to the graphics of desktops and laptops or to the GPUs of phones and tablets, and [`minYear` and `maxYear`](https://randino.cdget.com/gpu/rand-gpu#years) to the parts out in those years.

A graphics processor is written by its own name in every language, so `randGpu` takes no `language`.

```javascript
import { randGpu } from 'randino';

randGpu();
// ['NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060']
```

## Options

Every option is optional, and the defaults are what the empty call above uses.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `platform` | `SystemPlatformOption` | `'all'` | `desktop` for desktop cards, laptop GPUs and the graphics built into a PC processor, `mobile` for the GPUs of phones and tablets. `'all'` draws from both. |
| `minYear` | `number` | `—` | The earliest year a graphics processor may have come out in. See [years](https://randino.cdget.com/gpu/rand-gpu#years). |
| `maxYear` | `number` | `—` | The latest year a graphics processor may have come out in. See [years](https://randino.cdget.com/gpu/rand-gpu#years). |
| `vendor` | `GpuVendorOption` | `'all'` | Which makers, by the name each sells under: one, several, or every one of them. See [makers](https://randino.cdget.com/gpu/rand-gpu#vendors). |
| `includeVendor` | `boolean` | `true` | Write the maker in front: `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090` rather than `GeForce RTX 4090`. |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many graphics processors to return. Clamped to `0` … `10000`. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same graphics processor twice. Returns fewer than `count` once the catalog runs out. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or a `GpuDetail` per graphics processor. Dart has no such parameter — see [the detail output](https://randino.cdget.com/gpu/rand-gpu#the-detail-output). |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from — see [Choosing the source](https://randino.cdget.com/guide/getting-started#choosing-the-source). Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |

```javascript
randGpu({ platform: 'desktop', count: 3 }); // ['AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT', 'NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060', 'Intel UHD Graphics 630']
randGpu({ platform: 'mobile', count: 3 }); // ['Qualcomm Adreno 740', 'Arm Mali-G78', 'Samsung Xclipse 940']
randGpu({ includeVendor: false, count: 2 }); // ['Radeon RX 7900 XTX', 'GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU']
```

## What it draws from {#catalog}

179 graphics processors from the GeForce 8800 GTX in 2006 to the parts out by the end of 2025, every one of them as likely as the next once `platform` and the years have narrowed them:

| Platform | Maker | Parts | Years | Lines |
| --- | --- | --: | --- | --- |
| `desktop` | NVIDIA | 71 | 2006 – 2025 | GeForce 8 and 9, GeForce GTX, GeForce RTX, GeForce MX, the Laptop GPUs |
| `desktop` | ATI | 4 | 2008 – 2009 | Radeon HD 4000 and 5000 |
| `desktop` | AMD | 42 | 2010 – 2025 | Radeon HD, R9, RX, RX Vega, and the Radeon graphics built into Ryzen |
| `desktop` | Intel | 21 | 2011 – 2025 | HD, UHD, Iris and Arc |
| `mobile` | Qualcomm | 25 | 2013 – 2025 | Adreno |
| `mobile` | Arm | 13 | 2016 – 2024 | Mali and Immortalis |
| `mobile` | Samsung | 3 | 2022 – 2025 | Xclipse |

A Radeon from before the end of 2010 is written as ATI, because that is the name it was sold under; AMD retired the ATI name with the HD 6000 series. A laptop GPU is written the way NVIDIA writes it, `Laptop GPU` and all, so it is never mistaken for the desktop card of the same number. Apple's GPUs are left out: they carry no name of their own, and a Mac reports its chip's, which [`randCpu`](https://randino.cdget.com/cpu/rand-cpu) already writes.

The names are the products' own, and they belong to their owners. randino is not affiliated with any of them.

## Makers {#vendors}

`vendor` keeps to the makers named, written as the [catalog](https://randino.cdget.com/gpu/rand-gpu#catalog) writes them: `NVIDIA`, `ATI`, `AMD`, `Intel`, `Qualcomm`, `Arm` and `Samsung`, the order `GPU_VENDORS` lists them in. A name the catalog does not hold is ignored, and a list of nothing but such names draws every maker. It narrows alongside `platform` and the years, so a maker with no part there is answered with nothing: NVIDIA has no phone GPU here.

```javascript
randGpu({ vendor: 'NVIDIA', count: 2 }); // ['NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070', 'NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650']
randGpu({ vendor: ['AMD', 'ATI'], maxYear: 2010 }); // ['ATI Radeon HD 4870']
randGpu({ vendor: 'NVIDIA', platform: 'mobile' }); // []
```

## Years {#years}

The year of a graphics processor is the year the first cards or machines with it went on sale. `minYear` and `maxYear` keep to the parts out in that range, both years included. A range nothing came out in is answered with nothing, and a range the wrong way round keeps `maxYear`.

```javascript
randGpu({ platform: 'desktop', maxYear: 2010, count: 3 });
// ['ATI Radeon HD 4870', 'NVIDIA GeForce 8800 GT', 'NVIDIA GeForce GTX 480']

randGpu({ minYear: 2024, count: 2 }); // ['NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070', 'Qualcomm Adreno 830']
```

## The detail output {#the-detail-output}

The detail carries the maker and the model apart, so a result can be stored in two columns while the whole name is shown.

```javascript
randGpu({ output: 'detail' });
// [{ gpu: 'Intel Arc A770', vendor: 'Intel', model: 'Arc A770', platform: 'desktop', year: 2022 }]
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gpu` | `string` | The graphics processor, as the value form returns it. |
| `vendor` | `GpuVendor` | Who sells it under their name: `NVIDIA`, `AMD`, `Arm`. |
| `model` | `string` | The graphics processor's own name: `GeForce RTX 4090`. |
| `platform` | `SystemPlatform` | `desktop` or `mobile`. |
| `year` | `number` | The year the first cards or machines with it went on sale. |

## See also

- [`randCpu`](https://randino.cdget.com/cpu/rand-cpu) — the processor beside it.
- [`randDevice`](https://randino.cdget.com/device/rand-device) — a phone, a tablet or a laptop the graphics could be in.

# randArchitecture

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/architecture/rand-architecture

Generates processor architectures and returns `count` of them, by the name a download page most often lists them under: `x86_64`, `arm64`, `x86`, `armv7`. Nearly every machine runs one of these four, so they are all a draw returns until [`includeRare`](https://randino.cdget.com/architecture/rand-architecture#rare) adds the architectures few machines run, and those come up rarely even then. With [`output: 'detail'`](https://randino.cdget.com/architecture/rand-architecture#the-detail-output) it reports the other names each one goes by.

An architecture is written the same in every language, so `randArchitecture` takes none.

```javascript
import { randArchitecture } from 'randino';

randArchitecture();
// ['x86_64']
```

## Options

Every option is optional, and the defaults are what the empty call above uses.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `includeRare` | `boolean` | `false` | Draw the architectures few machines run as well, rarely. See [rare architectures](https://randino.cdget.com/architecture/rand-architecture#rare). |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many architectures to return. Clamped to `0` … `10000`. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same architecture twice. Returns fewer than `count` once they run out. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or an `ArchitectureDetail` per architecture. Dart has no such parameter — see [the detail output](https://randino.cdget.com/architecture/rand-architecture#the-detail-output). |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from — see [Choosing the source](https://randino.cdget.com/guide/getting-started#choosing-the-source). Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |

## How often each one comes up {#shares}

The shares are written by hand in the order the architectures are common in, not measured from any one survey: 64-bit x86 and Arm are nearly every desktop, laptop, phone and server, and the 32-bit two what is left of the older machines.

| Architecture | Also written | Bits | Share | With `includeRare` |
| --- | --- | --: | --: | --: |
| `x86_64` | `amd64`, `x64` | 64 | 46% | 43.9% |
| `arm64` | `aarch64` | 64 | 40% | 38.2% |
| `x86` | `i386`, `ia32`, `i686` | 32 | 8% | 7.6% |
| `armv7` | `armhf`, `armv7l` | 32 | 6% | 5.7% |
| `riscv64` | — | 64 | — | 0.8% |
| `ppc64le` | `ppc64el` | 64 | — | 0.8% |
| `s390x` | — | 64 | — | 0.8% |
| `mips64` | — | 64 | — | 0.8% |
| `loongarch64` | `loong64` | 64 | — | 0.8% |
| `sparc64` | `sparcv9` | 64 | — | 0.8% |

Each architecture is written by the name a download page most often lists it under. That is not always what a system reports: Linux's `uname -m` prints `aarch64` for `arm64`, `i686` for `x86` and `armv7l` for `armv7`, and Debian and Windows have names of their own. The other names are in the [detail](https://randino.cdget.com/architecture/rand-architecture#the-detail-output), so a result can be turned into whichever one a system expects.

## Rare architectures {#rare}

`includeRare` adds six architectures few machines run: RISC-V, POWER in its little-endian form, IBM Z, 64-bit MIPS, LoongArch and SPARC. Each is a draw in about a hundred and thirty, so a sample of fifty usually has none or one of them, and the four common ones keep their proportions beside them.

```javascript
randArchitecture({ count: 4 }); // ['x86_64', 'arm64', 'x86_64', 'armv7']
randArchitecture({ includeRare: true, count: 4 }); // ['arm64', 'x86_64', 'riscv64', 'x86_64']
randArchitecture({ includeRare: true, unique: true, count: 10 });
// ['x86_64', 'arm64', 'x86', 'armv7', 'ppc64le', 's390x', 'riscv64', 'mips64', 'sparc64', 'loongarch64']
```

## The detail output {#the-detail-output}

The detail carries the other names an architecture goes by, its width and the line it belongs to, so a result can be written the way Debian, Windows or Go expects it.

```javascript
randArchitecture({ output: 'detail' });
// [{ architecture: 'x86_64', aliases: ['amd64', 'x64'], bits: 64, family: 'x86', rare: false }]
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `architecture` | `Architecture` | The architecture, as the value form returns it. |
| `aliases` | `string[]` | The other names it goes by: Debian's and Go's first, then Windows' and Node's, then the kernel's or the compiler's. |
| `bits` | `number` | `32` or `64`. |
| `family` | `string` | The line it belongs to: `x86`, `arm`, `riscv`, `power`, `s390`, `mips`, `loongarch` or `sparc`. |
| `rare` | `boolean` | Whether it is one of the architectures `includeRare` adds. |

## See also

- [`randCpu`](https://randino.cdget.com/cpu/rand-cpu) — a processor that runs it.
- [`randOs`](https://randino.cdget.com/os/rand-os) — an operating system built for it.

---

# randResolution

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/resolution/rand-resolution

Generates screen resolutions and returns `count` of them, written as the width, an `x` and the height: `1920x1080`, `2560x1440`, `390x844`. They are the sizes people's screens really have, and the common ones come up most often — 1920x1080 is about a quarter of the desktops. [`platform`](https://randino.cdget.com/resolution/rand-resolution#platform) keeps to the screens of desktops and laptops or to those of phones and tablets, and [`separator`](https://randino.cdget.com/resolution/rand-resolution#separator) writes something else between the two numbers.

A resolution is written the same in every language, so `randResolution` takes no `language`.

```javascript
import { randResolution } from 'randino';

randResolution();
// ['1920x1080']
```

## Options

Every option is optional, and the defaults are what the empty call above uses.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `platform` | `SystemPlatformOption` | `'all'` | `desktop` for the screens of desktops and laptops, `mobile` for those of phones and tablets. `'all'` draws both evenly. See [platform](https://randino.cdget.com/resolution/rand-resolution#platform). |
| `separator` | `string` | `'x'` | What goes between the width and the height. See [the separator](https://randino.cdget.com/resolution/rand-resolution#separator). |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many resolutions to return. Clamped to `0` … `10000`. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same resolution twice. Returns fewer than `count` once they run out. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or a `ResolutionDetail` per resolution. Dart has no such parameter — see [the detail output](https://randino.cdget.com/resolution/rand-resolution#the-detail-output). |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from — see [Choosing the source](https://randino.cdget.com/guide/getting-started#choosing-the-source). Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |

## Platform {#platform}

A desktop screen is wider than it is tall, and a phone or a tablet is written portrait, its width first, the way a page in its browser sees it. Tablets count as `mobile`. Left out, a draw is a desktop half the time and a phone or a tablet the other half, however many sizes each of them lists.

```javascript
randResolution({ platform: 'desktop', count: 3 }); // ['1920x1080', '2560x1440', '1366x768']
randResolution({ platform: 'mobile', count: 3 }); // ['390x844', '360x800', '820x1180']
```

## How often each one comes up {#shares}

The sizes are the ones a browser reports for a screen. On a scaled display that is the size the system lays things out at rather than the panel's own pixels: a 1920x1080 laptop at 125% is `1536x864`, and a 14-inch MacBook Pro is `1512x982`. The shares are written by hand in the order the sizes are common in, not measured from any one survey, and each platform's add up to a hundred.

On a desktop or a laptop:

| Size        | Share |
| ----------- | ----: |
| `1920x1080` |   26% |
| `1366x768`  |   10% |
| `1536x864`  |   10% |
| `2560x1440` |    9% |
| `1440x900`  |    5% |
| `3840x2160` |    5% |
| `1280x720`  |    4% |
| `1600x900`  |    4% |
| `1280x800`  |    3% |
| `1680x1050` |    3% |
| `1920x1200` |    3% |
| `2560x1600` |    3% |
| `1470x956`  |    3% |
| `1512x982`  |    3% |
| `1280x1024` |    2% |
| `3440x1440` |    2% |
| `1728x1117` |    2% |
| `1024x768`  |    1% |
| `2560x1080` |    1% |
| `1360x768`  |    1% |

On a phone or a tablet, the phones first and the tablets after them:

| Size        | Share |
| ----------- | ----: |
| `360x800`   |   12% |
| `390x844`   |   10% |
| `412x915`   |    9% |
| `393x852`   |    8% |
| `414x896`   |    6% |
| `375x812`   |    5% |
| `375x667`   |    5% |
| `430x932`   |    5% |
| `393x873`   |    4% |
| `360x780`   |    4% |
| `428x926`   |    4% |
| `768x1024`  |    4% |
| `384x854`   |    3% |
| `360x740`   |    3% |
| `402x874`   |    3% |
| `810x1080`  |    3% |
| `440x956`   |    2% |
| `360x640`   |    2% |
| `820x1180`  |    2% |
| `834x1194`  |    2% |
| `800x1280`  |    2% |
| `320x568`   |    1% |
| `1024x1366` |    1% |

With `platform` left out, each share is half of what the table says.

## The separator {#separator}

`separator` replaces the `x` and may be any string, an empty one included. The [detail](https://randino.cdget.com/resolution/rand-resolution#the-detail-output) carries the two numbers apart whatever it is.

```javascript
randResolution({ separator: '×' }); // ['1920×1080']
randResolution({ separator: ' × ' }); // ['2560 × 1440']
randResolution({ separator: ',' }); // ['1366,768']
```

## The detail output {#the-detail-output}

The detail carries the width and the height as numbers, so a result can be used without being split again.

```javascript
randResolution({ output: 'detail' });
// [{ resolution: '1920x1080', width: 1920, height: 1080, platform: 'desktop' }]
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resolution` | `string` | The resolution, as the value form returns it. |
| `width` | `number` | The width, in the pixels a browser reports. |
| `height` | `number` | The height, in the pixels a browser reports. |
| `platform` | `SystemPlatform` | `desktop` or `mobile`. |

## See also

- [`randDevice`](https://randino.cdget.com/device/rand-device) — a phone, a tablet or a laptop the screen could belong to.
- [`randOs`](https://randino.cdget.com/os/rand-os) — an operating system to go with it.

# randVersion

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/version/rand-version

Generates software version numbers and returns `count` of them, in one of three [formats](https://randino.cdget.com/version/rand-version#formats): a semantic version (`2.14.3`), a calendar version counted from a year (`2024.3.1`, `24.04`), or a single number (`42`). Every part is drawn with the [small numbers most often](https://randino.cdget.com/version/rand-version#parts), so `0.x` and `x.y.0` come up the way they do in a package registry. [`prefix`](https://randino.cdget.com/version/rand-version#prefix) writes something such as `v` in front, and [`includePrerelease`](https://randino.cdget.com/version/rand-version#prerelease) gives a semantic version a `-beta.2` now and then.

Unlike the other system values, a version is drawn rather than picked from a catalog: no list of the world's version numbers exists, and any version here may belong to some real release by chance. A version is written the same in every language, so `randVersion` takes no `language`.

```javascript
import { randVersion } from 'randino';

randVersion();
// ['2.14.3']
```

## Options

Every option is optional, and the defaults are what the empty call above uses.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | `VersionFormatOption` | `'semver'` | How the version is numbered: one format, several drawn evenly one per result, or every one of them with `'all'`. See [formats](https://randino.cdget.com/version/rand-version#formats). |
| `prefix` | `string` | `''` | Written in front of every version. See [the prefix](https://randino.cdget.com/version/rand-version#prefix). |
| `includePrerelease` | `boolean` | `false` | Give about one semantic version in four a pre-release. See [pre-releases](https://randino.cdget.com/version/rand-version#prerelease). |
| `minYear` | `number` | `2010` | The earliest year a calendar version may be counted from. See [years](https://randino.cdget.com/version/rand-version#years). |
| `maxYear` | `number` | `2026` | The latest year a calendar version may be counted from. See [years](https://randino.cdget.com/version/rand-version#years). |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many versions to return. Clamped to `0` … `10000`. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same version twice. Returns fewer than `count` once they run out. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or a `VersionDetail` per version. Dart has no such parameter — see [the detail output](https://randino.cdget.com/version/rand-version#the-detail-output). |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from — see [Choosing the source](https://randino.cdget.com/guide/getting-started#choosing-the-source). Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |

The default is `semver` rather than every format, because a column of versions is usually one scheme.

## Formats {#formats}

| Format | Scheme | Example | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `semver` | `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` | `2.14.3` | Semantic versioning, the scheme most package registries use |
| `calver` | `YYYY.MINOR` | `2024.2` | A year and the release within it |
| `calver` | `YYYY.MM.MICRO` | `2024.3.1` | A year, a month and a fix |
| `calver` | `YY.0M` | `24.04` | A short year and a zero-padded month |
| `calver` | `YY.0M.MICRO` | `24.04.1` | The same with a fix |
| `calver` | `YYYY.0M.0D` | `2024.03.15` | A whole date |
| `number` | `MAJOR` | `42` | A version that is one number, the way a browser's is |

The schemes are written in [CalVer](https://calver.org)'s notation, where `YY` is the year less 2000 and `MINOR` in a calendar scheme is the release within the year. A calendar version draws a scheme by weight — the first two a quarter each, `YY.0M` a fifth, the last two fifteen percent each — and a date it writes is always a real day.

```javascript
randVersion({ format: 'calver', count: 3 }); // ['2024.3.1', '24.04', '2019.2']
randVersion({ format: 'number', count: 3 }); // ['42', '3', '118']
randVersion({ format: ['semver', 'number'], count: 3 }); // ['1.4.0', '7', '0.12.2']
randVersion({ format: 'all', count: 3 }); // ['2.0.1', '2023.11.2', '15']
```

## How the numbers are drawn {#parts}

Each number is drawn from a range, and a number comes up about twice as often as the one twice as far from the bottom of it. The bottom of a range is the most common value, and the top is rare.

| Part | Range | The bottom of it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Semantic major | `0` … `20` | About a quarter of the versions are `0.x` |
| Semantic minor and patch | `0` … `30` | About a quarter end on `.0` |
| Single number | `1` … `150` | Half of them are `9` or less |
| Calendar release within a year (`MINOR`) | `1` … `4` | About half are the year's first |
| Calendar fix (`MICRO`) | `1` … `9` | About a third are the first fix |
| Pre-release number | `1` … `9` | About a third are the first |

## The prefix {#prefix}

`prefix` is written in front of every version, whatever its format. The [detail](https://randino.cdget.com/version/rand-version#the-detail-output) keeps the numbers apart from it.

```javascript
randVersion({ prefix: 'v' }); // ['v2.14.3']
randVersion({ format: 'calver', prefix: 'release-' }); // ['release-24.04']
```

## Pre-releases {#prerelease}

`includePrerelease` gives about one semantic version in four a pre-release, written the way semantic versioning writes it: a hyphen, a label and a number. The label is `alpha` 30% of the time, `beta` 35% and `rc` 35%. Calendar and single-number versions never carry one.

```javascript
randVersion({ includePrerelease: true, count: 4 });
// ['1.4.0', '3.0.0-rc.1', '0.12.2', '2.1.0-beta.2']
```

## Years {#years}

`minYear` and `maxYear` keep a calendar version to the years between them, both included, and every year is as likely as the next. Left out, the range is 2010 to 2026. It is fixed rather than counted from today, so a seeded `random` gives the same versions on every run. A bound left out moves out of the way of the one that was written, so `minYear: 2030` alone is 2030, and a range the wrong way round keeps `maxYear`. Every year is kept inside 2000 to 2099, because the short year is the year less 2000. The two options do nothing to the other formats.

## The detail output {#the-detail-output}

The detail carries the scheme and the numbers a version is made of, so a result can be compared or sorted without being parsed again.

```javascript
randVersion({ format: 'calver', output: 'detail' });
// [{ version: '24.04', format: 'calver', scheme: 'YY.0M', parts: [24, 4], prerelease: null, year: 2024 }]
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `string` | The version, as the value form returns it, prefix included. |
| `format` | `VersionFormat` | `semver`, `calver` or `number`. |
| `scheme` | `string` | How it is numbered, in CalVer's notation: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, `MAJOR`, `YY.0M`. |
| `parts` | `number[]` | The numbers in the order they are written. A short year is written as it is, `24`. |
| `prerelease` | `string &#124; null` | The pre-release without its hyphen, `beta.2`, or none. |
| `year` | `number &#124; null` | The full year a calendar version is counted from, or none for the other formats. |

## See also

- [`randOs`](https://randino.cdget.com/os/rand-os) — an operating system, with a real version of its own.
- [`randDate`](https://randino.cdget.com/date/rand-date) — a date, for the day a version was released.

---

# randAppStore

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/appstore/rand-app-store

Generates real app stores and returns `count` of them, by the name each is known by, with its company in front where the store is called by one: `Google Play Store`, `Apple App Store`, `Samsung Galaxy Store`, `Steam`. The common stores come up most often. [`platform`](https://randino.cdget.com/appstore/rand-app-store#catalog) keeps to the stores of phones and tablets or to those of desktops and laptops, and Google Play is never a desktop's.

A store is called by its own name in every language, so `randAppStore` takes no `language`.

```javascript
import { randAppStore } from 'randino';

randAppStore();
// ['Google Play Store']
```

## Options

Every option is optional, and the defaults are what the empty call above uses.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `platform` | `SystemPlatformOption` | `'all'` | `mobile` for the stores of phones and tablets, `desktop` for those of desktops and laptops. `'all'` draws both evenly. |
| `includeCompany` | `boolean` | `true` | Write the company in front where the store is called by one: `Apple App Store` rather than `App Store`. A store whose name carries no company is written the same either way. |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many stores to return. Clamped to `0` … `10000`. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same store twice. Returns fewer than `count` once the catalog runs out. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or an `AppStoreDetail` per store. Dart has no such parameter — see [the detail output](https://randino.cdget.com/appstore/rand-app-store#the-detail-output). |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from — see [Choosing the source](https://randino.cdget.com/guide/getting-started#choosing-the-source). Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |

```javascript
randAppStore({ platform: 'mobile', count: 3 }); // ['Google Play Store', 'Apple App Store', 'Huawei AppGallery']
randAppStore({ platform: 'desktop', count: 3 }); // ['Steam', 'Microsoft Store', 'Mac App Store']
randAppStore({ includeCompany: false, count: 2 }); // ['App Store', 'Galaxy Store']
```

## What it draws from {#catalog}

Eighteen stores, each one still open. The platform is drawn first, so with `platform` left out half the results are each, and the shares below are then halved. The shares are written by hand in the order the stores are common in, not measured from any one survey.

On a phone or a tablet, the system's own and the makers' stores first, and the independent ones that ship by themselves after them:

| Store                  | Own name          | Company   | Share |
| ---------------------- | ----------------- | --------- | ----: |
| `Google Play Store`    | `Google Play`     | Google    |   45% |
| `Apple App Store`      | `App Store`       | Apple     |   35% |
| `Samsung Galaxy Store` | `Galaxy Store`    | Samsung   |    6% |
| `Huawei AppGallery`    | `AppGallery`      | Huawei    |    5% |
| `Amazon Appstore`      | `Amazon Appstore` | Amazon    |    3% |
| `Xiaomi GetApps`       | `GetApps`         | Xiaomi    |    2% |
| `ONE store`            | `ONE store`       | ONE store |    2% |
| `Aptoide`              | `Aptoide`         | Aptoide   |    1% |
| `F-Droid`              | `F-Droid`         | F-Droid   |    1% |

On a desktop or a laptop, the system stores and the stores games are bought from:

| Store              | Own name           | Company         | Share |
| ------------------ | ------------------ | --------------- | ----: |
| `Microsoft Store`  | `Microsoft Store`  | Microsoft       |   30% |
| `Steam`            | `Steam`            | Valve           |   25% |
| `Mac App Store`    | `Mac App Store`    | Apple           |   20% |
| `Epic Games Store` | `Epic Games Store` | Epic Games      |    8% |
| `GOG.com`          | `GOG.com`          | GOG             |    4% |
| `Snap Store`       | `Snap Store`       | Canonical       |    4% |
| `EA app`           | `EA app`           | Electronic Arts |    3% |
| `Ubisoft Connect`  | `Ubisoft Connect`  | Ubisoft         |    3% |
| `Setapp`           | `Setapp`           | MacPaw          |    3% |

Google Play is in the first table alone: no desktop system ships it. The names are the stores' own, and they belong to their owners. randino is not affiliated with any of them.

## The detail output {#the-detail-output}

The detail carries the store's own name and the company apart, so a result can be stored in two columns while the whole name is shown.

```javascript
randAppStore({ output: 'detail' });
// [{ store: 'Samsung Galaxy Store', name: 'Galaxy Store', company: 'Samsung', platform: 'mobile' }]
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `store` | `string` | The store, as the value form returns it. |
| `name` | `string` | The store's own name, without the company: `Galaxy Store`. |
| `company` | `string` | The company that runs it: `Samsung`. |
| `platform` | `SystemPlatform` | `desktop` or `mobile`. |

## See also

- [`randOs`](https://randino.cdget.com/os/rand-os) — the operating system a store sells apps for.
- [`randDevice`](https://randino.cdget.com/device/rand-device) — a phone, a tablet or a laptop to install from it.
- [`randVersion`](https://randino.cdget.com/version/rand-version) — the version of an app it lists.

# randFileExtension

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/file/rand-file-extension

Generates file extensions and returns `count` of them, each one an extension files are really saved with: `.pdf`, `.png`, `.mp4`, `.zip`, `.js`. The extensions nearly everybody meets come up most often, and the ones only a few programs write rarely. [`category`](https://randino.cdget.com/file/rand-file-extension#catalog) keeps to one kind of file or several, and `includeDot` leaves the dot out.

An extension is written the same in every language, so `randFileExtension` takes no `language`.

```javascript
import { randFileExtension } from 'randino';

randFileExtension();
// ['.pdf']
```

## Options

Every option is optional, and the defaults are what the empty call above uses.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `category` | `FileCategoryOption` | `'all'` | Which kinds of file: one category, several, or every one of them. See [the catalog](https://randino.cdget.com/file/rand-file-extension#catalog). |
| `includeDot` | `boolean` | `true` | Write the dot in front: `.png` rather than `png`. |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many extensions to return. Clamped to `0` … `10000`. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same extension twice. Returns fewer than `count` once they run out. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or a `FileExtensionDetail` per extension. Dart has no such parameter — see [the detail output](https://randino.cdget.com/file/rand-file-extension#the-detail-output). |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from — see [Choosing the source](https://randino.cdget.com/guide/getting-started#choosing-the-source). Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |

```javascript
randFileExtension({ count: 3 }); // ['.pdf', '.png', '.mp4']
randFileExtension({ category: 'image', count: 3 }); // ['.png', '.jpg', '.webp']
randFileExtension({ category: ['code', 'data'], includeDot: false, count: 3 }); // ['js', 'json', 'py']
```

## What it draws from {#catalog}

136 extensions in fourteen categories, every one written in lower case and every one in a single category. An extension that could mean two things is the one a developer means by it: `.ts` is TypeScript rather than an MPEG stream, and `.sql` is data. Two spellings of one format are both in where both are in use, such as `.jpg` and `.jpeg`.

Each extension has a weight from `5` for the ones nearly everybody meets to `1` for the ones only a few programs write, and the draw is over the extensions themselves rather than one category at a time. `.pdf`, one of the commonest, is about one draw in fifty.

| Category | What it holds | Weight 5–3 | Weight 2 | Weight 1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `document` | Documents | `.pdf`, `.docx`, `.txt` | `.doc`, `.rtf`, `.odt`, `.md` | `.tex`, `.pages`, `.wpd` |
| `spreadsheet` | Spreadsheets | `.xlsx`, `.csv` | `.xls`, `.ods` | `.numbers`, `.tsv` |
| `presentation` | Presentations | `.pptx` | — | `.ppt`, `.odp`, `.key` |
| `image` | Images | `.jpg`, `.png`, `.gif`, `.svg`, `.webp`, `.jpeg` | `.heic`, `.bmp`, `.tiff`, `.ico` | `.psd`, `.avif`, `.tif`, `.ai`, `.eps`, `.dng` |
| `audio` | Audio | `.mp3` | `.wav`, `.m4a`, `.aac`, `.flac`, `.ogg` | `.wma`, `.aiff`, `.opus`, `.mid` |
| `video` | Video | `.mp4` | `.mov`, `.avi`, `.mkv`, `.webm` | `.wmv`, `.flv`, `.m4v`, `.3gp`, `.mpeg` |
| `archive` | Archives | `.zip` | `.rar`, `.7z`, `.gz`, `.tar` | `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.tgz`, `.zst` |
| `code` | Source code | `.js`, `.html`, `.css`, `.py` | `.ts`, `.java`, `.c`, `.cpp`, `.php`, `.go`, `.rs`, `.rb`, `.swift`, `.kt`, `.sh`, `.cs` | `.h`, `.hpp`, `.scala`, `.lua`, `.pl`, `.r`, `.dart`, `.vue`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`, `.bat`, `.ps1` |
| `data` | Data and configuration | `.json`, `.xml` | `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.sql`, `.db`, `.sqlite`, `.log` | `.toml`, `.ini`, `.cfg`, `.plist`, `.parquet` |
| `executable` | Programs and installers | `.exe`, `.apk` | `.msi`, `.dmg`, `.ipa`, `.deb`, `.rpm` | `.jar`, `.bin`, `.appimage`, `.msix` |
| `font` | Fonts | — | `.ttf`, `.otf`, `.woff2` | `.woff`, `.eot` |
| `ebook` | E-books | — | `.epub` | `.mobi`, `.azw3` |
| `disk` | Disk images | — | `.iso` | `.img`, `.vhd`, `.vmdk`, `.qcow2` |
| `model` | 3D models | — | — | `.stl`, `.obj`, `.fbx`, `.glb`, `.gltf`, `.blend` |

The weights are written by hand in the order the extensions are common in, not measured from any one survey.

## The detail output {#the-detail-output}

The detail carries the extension without its dot, the kind of file it is and the MIME type it is served as.

```javascript
randFileExtension({ output: 'detail' });
// [{ extension: '.png', name: 'png', category: 'image', mimeType: 'image/png' }]
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extension` | `string` | The extension, as the value form returns it. |
| `name` | `string` | The extension without its dot: `png`. |
| `category` | `FileCategory` | The kind of file it is: `image`. |
| `mimeType` | `string` | The MIME type a file with it is served as: `image/png`. See [`randMimeType`](https://randino.cdget.com/file/rand-mime-type#source) for where the types come from. |

## See also

- [`randWord`](https://randino.cdget.com/word/rand-word) — a word to name the file with.
- [`randMimeType`](https://randino.cdget.com/file/rand-mime-type) — the MIME types these extensions are served as.
- [`randAppStore`](https://randino.cdget.com/appstore/rand-app-store) — a store to get a program from.

---

# randMimeType

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/file/rand-mime-type

Generates MIME types and returns `count` of them, each one a type files are really served as: `application/pdf`, `image/png`, `video/mp4`. They are the types [`randFileExtension`](https://randino.cdget.com/file/rand-file-extension)'s extensions carry, once each, and a type is as common as its most common extension. [`type`](https://randino.cdget.com/file/rand-mime-type#types) keeps to the top-level types named, the part in front of the slash.

A MIME type is written the same in every language, so `randMimeType` takes no `language`.

```javascript
import { randMimeType } from 'randino';

randMimeType();
// ['application/pdf']
```

## Options

Every option is optional, and the defaults are what the empty call above uses.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `MimeTopLevelOption` | `'all'` | Which top-level types: one, several, or every one of them. See [top-level types](https://randino.cdget.com/file/rand-mime-type#types). |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many types to return. Clamped to `0` … `10000`. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same type twice. Returns fewer than `count` once they run out. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or a `MimeTypeDetail` per type. Dart has no such parameter — see [the detail output](https://randino.cdget.com/file/rand-mime-type#the-detail-output). |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from — see [Choosing the source](https://randino.cdget.com/guide/getting-started#choosing-the-source). Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |

## Top-level types {#types}

The part in front of the slash is one of seven, and each holds the types of the extensions that are served as it:

| Top-level type | Types | Share | Examples                                                 |
| -------------- | ----: | ----: | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `application`  |    52 |   48% | `application/pdf`, `application/zip`, `application/json` |
| `audio`        |     9 |    9% | `audio/mpeg`, `audio/wav`                                |
| `font`         |     4 |    4% | `font/woff2`, `font/ttf`                                 |
| `image`        |    12 |   15% | `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/svg+xml`               |
| `model`        |     4 |    2% | `model/gltf-binary`, `model/stl`                         |
| `text`         |    12 |   15% | `text/plain`, `text/html`, `text/csv`                    |
| `video`        |    10 |    9% | `video/mp4`, `video/webm`                                |

```javascript
randMimeType({ type: 'image', count: 3 }); // ['image/png', 'image/jpeg', 'image/webp']
randMimeType({ type: ['audio', 'video'], count: 2 }); // ['audio/mpeg', 'video/mp4']
```

## Where the types come from {#source}

Each extension carries the type [mime-db](https://github.com/jshttp/mime-db) 1.54.0 gives it. mime-db is the list web servers and their libraries serve files by, gathered from IANA, Apache and nginx. Where it gives an extension several types, the one IANA registered is used, and a specific type is preferred over `application/octet-stream`. Five extensions mime-db does not map take the type IANA registered for their format: `.zst`, `.sqlite`, `.parquet`, `.tgz` and `.azw3`.

An extension with no settled type is `text/plain` when the file is text and `application/octet-stream` when it is binary. Most of the source code is in the first group: `.ts`, `.go`, `.rs`, `.py` and others have no registered type, and mime-db's `video/mp2t` for `.ts` belongs to another format. Because a dozen extensions share `text/plain`, a type is as common as its most common extension rather than all of them together, so `text/plain` comes up no more often than `.txt` makes it.

## The detail output {#the-detail-output}

The detail splits the type at its slash and lists the extensions a file of it is saved with.

```javascript
randMimeType({ output: 'detail' });
// [{ mimeType: 'image/jpeg', type: 'image', subtype: 'jpeg', extensions: ['jpg', 'jpeg'] }]
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mimeType` | `string` | The type, as the value form returns it. |
| `type` | `MimeTopLevel` | The part in front of the slash: `image`. |
| `subtype` | `string` | The part behind it: `jpeg`. |
| `extensions` | `string[]` | The extensions a file of it is saved with, without their dots. |

## See also

- [`randFileExtension`](https://randino.cdget.com/file/rand-file-extension) — the extensions these types come from, each with its type in the detail.

---

# randCountry

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-country

Generates country names and returns `count` of them as strings: every country and territory ISO 3166-1 gives a code, 249 of them, named the way the language names it. With [`output: 'detail'`](https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-country#the-detail-output) it reports the code each one is known by.

Every word language has a name for every country, so this takes any of the nine, where [`randLocation`](https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-location) and the other level functions write only the languages whose countries publish their divisions.

```javascript
import { randCountry } from 'randino';

randCountry({ language: 'ko', count: 3 }); // ['아르헨티나', '방글라데시', '세인트키츠 네비스']
randCountry({ language: 'en', count: 2 }); // ['Gibraltar', 'Burkina Faso']
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | `WordLanguageOption` | `'all'` | Language the country names are written in, any of the nine. Left out, it picks one per result and mixes them. |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many results to return. Clamped to 0 … 10000. |
| `minLength` | `number` | _no bound_ | Minimum length in characters, of the whole string returned. |
| `maxLength` | `number` | _no bound_ | Maximum length in characters. A range nothing fits is answered with the closest length there is. |
| `startsWith` | `string` | `—` | Keep only results whose first character is this one. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same result twice. Returns fewer than asked once the list runs out. |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from. Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or one CountryDetail per result. |

## Which countries {#which-countries}

The list is ISO 3166-1's, as the tz database carries it: sovereign states and the territories ISO codes on their own, such as Greenland, Hong Kong and Antarctica. Codes ISO only reserves, such as `XK`, are not in it. Any list of countries is a position on a few places, and following the standard every country picker already uses is the one that can be explained without taking a new one.

The names are Wikidata's labels in each language. They are the names the language's own encyclopedia uses, so they mix common and official forms the way that encyclopedia does: `대한민국` beside `미국`, `США` in Russian. A name that starts in lower case mid-sentence is written with a capital, and the one country with no label in a language, Jersey in Vietnamese, Spanish, Italian and German, is written the way those languages write it, `Jersey`.

Every country is drawn as often as any other. `unique` compares the names, so `language: 'all'` with `unique` stops at the names that differ, and `Andorra` counts once however many languages spell it that way.

## The detail output {#the-detail-output}

```javascript
randCountry({ language: 'ja', output: 'detail' });
// [{ country: 'サウジアラビア', code: 'SA', language: 'ja' }]
```

`code` is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, which is the same whatever the language the name is in.

## See also

- [`randLocation`](https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-location) — a place inside the language's own country, with the country on top.
- [`randRegion`](https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-region) — the level below the country.

---

# randRegion

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-region

A country's first-level divisions: a Korean 시·도, or a US state or the District of Columbia. Each is drawn as often as any other, whatever its size.

[`randLocation`](https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-location) with `level` fixed to `'region'`, handing back the division's name alone rather than the whole location.

```javascript
import { randRegion } from 'randino';

randRegion({ language: 'ko', count: 3 }); // ['세종특별자치시', '울산광역시', '강원특별자치도']
randRegion({ language: 'en', count: 3 }); // ['Idaho', 'Georgia', 'Vermont']
randRegion({ language: 'en', output: 'detail' });
// [{ location: 'Arkansas', language: 'en', level: 'region',
//    country: 'United States', region: 'Arkansas', city: null, district: null }]
```

Korea has sixteen of them and the United States fifty-one, so `unique: true` with a larger `count` returns every one and stops there.

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | `LocationLanguageOption` | `'all'` | Which language, and so which country, the places are from. Left out, it picks one per result and mixes them. |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many results to return. Clamped to 0 … 10000. |
| `minLength` | `number` | _no bound_ | Minimum length in characters, of the whole string returned. |
| `maxLength` | `number` | _no bound_ | Maximum length in characters. A range nothing fits is answered with the closest length there is. |
| `startsWith` | `string` | `—` | Keep only results whose first character is this one. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same result twice. Returns fewer than asked once the list runs out. |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from. Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or one LocationDetail per result. |

## See also

- [`randLocation`](https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-location) — the region with the country above it and the divisions below.
- [`randCity`](https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-city) — the level below the region.

---

# randCity

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-city

The divisions a region is made of: a Korean 시·군·구, or a US city, town, village or census designated place.

[`randLocation`](https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-location) with `level` fixed to `'city'`, handing back the division's name alone rather than the whole location.

```javascript
import { randCity } from 'randino';

randCity({ language: 'ko', count: 3 }); // ['함안군', '영덕군', '여수시']
randCity({ language: 'en', count: 3 }); // ['Donora', 'Blue Ridge', 'Chesilhurst']
randCity({ language: 'ko', output: 'detail' });
// [{ location: '중랑구', language: 'ko', level: 'city',
//    country: '대한민국', region: '서울특별시', city: '중랑구', district: null }]
```

A Korean 구 that is one of a city's districts rather than a local government of its own is written with its city, the way an address writes it: `수원시 장안구`, not `장안구`. 세종특별자치시 has no 시·군·구 at all, so it never comes back from here.

The same name can come back from different regions — Korea has a `중구` in five of them and twenty-eight US states have a `Franklin` — and `unique` compares the names, not the places. The detail output says which region each one is in.

```javascript
randCity({ language: 'ko', startsWith: '수', count: 3 }); // ['수영구', '수성구', '수원시 장안구']
randCity({ language: 'en', maxLength: 5, count: 3 }); // ['Loco', 'Bruin', 'Keota']
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | `LocationLanguageOption` | `'all'` | Which language, and so which country, the places are from. Left out, it picks one per result and mixes them. |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many results to return. Clamped to 0 … 10000. |
| `minLength` | `number` | _no bound_ | Minimum length in characters, of the whole string returned. |
| `maxLength` | `number` | _no bound_ | Maximum length in characters. A range nothing fits is answered with the closest length there is. |
| `startsWith` | `string` | `—` | Keep only results whose first character is this one. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same result twice. Returns fewer than asked once the list runs out. |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from. Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or one LocationDetail per result. |

## See also

- [`randLocation`](https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-location) — the city with the region and country above it.
- [`randDistrict`](https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-district) — the level below the city, which only Korea has.

---

# randDistrict

Source: https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-district

The divisions inside a city: a Korean 읍·면·동. It is the legal 동 an address is written with rather than the administrative 동 a community centre serves, and never the 리 below a 읍 or 면.

[`randLocation`](https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-location) with `level` fixed to `'district'`, handing back the division's name alone rather than the whole location.

```javascript
import { randDistrict } from 'randino';

randDistrict({ language: 'ko', count: 3 }); // ['가현동', '겸면', '행주외동']
randDistrict({ startsWith: '역', count: 3 }); // ['역북동', '역동', '역곡동']
randDistrict({ output: 'detail' });
// [{ location: '차황면', language: 'ko', level: 'district',
//    country: '대한민국', region: '경상남도', city: '산청군', district: '차황면' }]
```

Only Korean locations have this level. Asking for English returns nothing, and leaving `language` out draws Korean rather than spending half the draws on a country that has no districts.

```javascript
randDistrict({ language: 'en' }); // []
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | `LocationLanguageOption` | `'all'` | Which language, and so which country, the places are from. Left out, it picks one per result and mixes them. |
| `count` | `number` | `1` | How many results to return. Clamped to 0 … 10000. |
| `minLength` | `number` | _no bound_ | Minimum length in characters, of the whole string returned. |
| `maxLength` | `number` | _no bound_ | Maximum length in characters. A range nothing fits is answered with the closest length there is. |
| `startsWith` | `string` | `—` | Keep only results whose first character is this one. |
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Never return the same result twice. Returns fewer than asked once the list runs out. |
| `random` | `() => number` | `—` | Where the randomness comes from. Defaults to the platform's ordinary generator. |
| `output` | `RandOutput` | `'value'` | Strings, or one LocationDetail per result. |

## See also

- [`randLocation`](https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-location) — the district with every level above it.
- [`randCity`](https://randino.cdget.com/location/rand-city) — the level above the district.
